overall: Washington, DC is running very warm this afternoon, with a current observed temperature of 87.8°F as of 1:45 PM ET — already within striking distance of the NWS forecast high of ~89°F. A tropical air mass is firmly in place (dewpoint 75.2°F, Flood Watch active), supporting continued warmth but also fueling afternoon convection; scattered thunderstorms with 50% PoP are the primary wild card for the remainder of the heating window. Skies have partially broken from OVC to BKN, but a low 610m ceiling and active storm development nearby will likely limit further significant temperature gains.
forecast_obs_notes: Model consensus is tighter than average at the top: ECMWF (88.6°F), GFS (87.8°F), and NWS (~89°F) cluster in the 87–89°F range, while HRRR (90.2°F with a suspicious 20:00h peak) is an outlier likely reflecting delayed convective mixing that may not verify. The META fused model places the highest probability on the 88–89°F even bucket (35%), meaningfully below D1_NOW's top pick of 90–91°F (40.8%), suggesting observational evidence is pulling the distribution slightly cooler than the raw NWP ensemble.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 87.8°F and a still-positive warming velocity of +3.6°F/hr, the temperature has room to climb another 0.5–1.5°F before peak (predicted ~14:12 ET), but incoming convective cloud cover and likely thunderstorm initiation will cap further gains. The 88–89°F even bucket is the most probable landing zone, supported by NWS guidance (~89°F), ECMWF (88.6°F), and the META model (35% weight), with moderate confidence; the 90–91°F bucket remains plausible (~25–30% effective odds) if convection holds off and skies clear briefly, but the tropical flood-watch environment argues against a clean afternoon heating window.
